concerns.text: Phase 6 tasks introduce a 'Scaling Law' module (T034-T037, T060-T062) based on urban theory (Bettencourt et al.) and 'universal scaling exponents'. The spec (Assumptions) explicitly limits scope to 'US context' using 'PSM/DiD on RECS/ACS microdata'. This module constitutes unauthorized scope creep and violates the constitutional principle of Causal Identification Rigor (Section VI) by introducing a descriptive framework not mandated by the spec, risking conflation of descriptive gaps with causal impacts.

FR-008 mandates a fallback to Difference-in-Differences (DiD) if PSM fails. Tasks T053 (control flow) and T054 (DiD fallback logic) are marked incomplete/unchecked. Without these, the system cannot satisfy the fallback requirement, violating the spec's core causal identification strategy.

FR-009 requires a placebo test to validate the unconfoundedness assumption. Task T025 implements the logic, but T046 (pipeline execution/gating) is unchecked. The system lacks the enforcement mechanism to halt or trigger fallback if the placebo test fails, violating the acceptance criteria for US-2.

FR-006 requires a sensitivity analysis sweeping the PSM caliper for the *causal* ATT estimate. Phase 6 tasks (T034-T037) implement a sensitivity analysis for a *descriptive* scaling law exponent. The tasks lack any mechanism to sweep the PSM caliper for the causal estimate as required by FR-006, effectively weakening the requirement.

Constitution Section IV (Single Source of Truth) and Section VI (Causal Identification Rigor) require strict separation of causal and descriptive findings. Tasks T045 (Final report) and T051 (Report generator logic) are unchecked, creating a high risk that the final report will conflate descriptive scaling gaps with causal impacts.

Constitution Section I (Reproducibility) requires a reproducible environment. Tasks T001 (project structure), T003 (linting), and T004 (pytest config) are unchecked. Without these, the project cannot guarantee reproducibility on a fresh runner, violating the non-negotiable constitutional principle.
